label: Late original-phase inputs and <DEL> (not input a)
explanation: Fires during the input-reading part of the sequence: original-phase steps from t>=2 (mostly t>=3) and the <DEL> step (rate 0.75 at <DEL>). Silent at t=0,1 and essentially silent through the whole copy phase (0.1% rate, ~0 mass). Activation rate and magnitude grow with position in the original sequence (rate 0.31 at orig_idx 2 to ~0.86 at orig_idx 6); the strongest activations are late original steps and <DEL> in short-to-mid sequences, often ramping step by step up to <DEL>. Input token modulates it: input a strongly suppresses it (precision 0.15 vs ~0.74 for i/z/3), and l/k/q/n/w are weaker; repeated tokens (in_first=0) are less active. It does not fire on copy-phase outputs. Remaining false positives are mostly whole sequences that stay low, apparently set by token content.

issues: The factual claim that repeated tokens (in_first=0) are less active is wrong. The overall 0.066 rate for in_first=0 comes from the copy phase. Restricted to original-phase steps with t>=2, in_first=0 has precision 0.69, above the ~0.62 base rate for those steps. Adding in_first==1 to the predicate lowers F1 from 0.81 to 0.76.

The explanation treats the false positives as unexplained whole sequences that stay low because of which tokens they contain. In fact there is a clear systematic history effect: which tokens appeared earlier in the sequence. With the base (phase<=1)&(t>=3), seen(tok) precision is 0.51 for a, 0.55 for y and q, 0.60 for l, 0.62 for k, 0.64 for w and 0.65 for n. For i, t, u, z, 3 and similar tokens it is 0.83-0.85. Test misses show silent runs such as 'q u k k k r a g', 'l q w m', 'p l o r k y t' and 'z l c r o k 3 d'.

The label puts the token dependence on the current input token only (not 'a'). The bigger effect is the prefix: how many of the suppressing tokens {a,q,y,l,k,w,n} came before this step. The explanation lists l,k,q,n,w only as weaker current inputs and does not mention y at all.
The predicate sits at the threshold (test F1 0.81, precision 0.73), and a simple history-aware predicate does better on both splits: dev F1 0.846, test F1 0.846, precision 0.857, recall 0.836.

Claims that check out: the feature is silent at t=0 and t=1. In the copy phase it fires on 0.1% of steps with about 0 activation mass. It fires 75% of the time at <DEL>. Its firing rate rises with orig_idx (0.31 at idx 2, 0.86 at idx 6). Input 'a' as the current token gives precision 0.15.
